newsitem.title: USA: Consumers pushes Mich. nuke restart to Weds.
newsitem.headline: Consumers pushes Mich. nuke restart to Weds.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Wednesday it pushed back the restart of its Palisades nuclear power plant to late today from original restart expectations for Tuesday because it needed time for startup testing.
"We expect it to return to service tonight. It's just taking more time for the air compression test," a company spokesman said.
Consumers decided to fully shut the 780 megawatt plant early Monday after discovery of a hydrogen leak on the unit's main generator, where hydrogen is used as a cooling agent.
The unit, located in South Haven, Mich., was operating at about half power late last week due to a vibration in the isphase bus.
Consumers Energy is a subsidiary of CMS Energy Corp.
